name: Permadeath Flag
description: The opt-in contract that turns a defeat into a funeral. When enabled, a combat.entityDefeated on a player unit is not a knockout — the unit leaves the roster, its gear returns to inventory.core_inventory, and the loss is written through persistence.save_system immediately, because a permadeath that only exists until the next save is one reload away from meaning nothing. This component owns the policy and its irrevocability. It does not own the death itself — combat.damage_resolver decided that — and it does not own the memorial: it emits the loss and lets the game decide whether the fallen get a graveyard, a statue, or a line in the credits. Off by default, because permadeath is a mode a player chooses, not a surprise a tutorial springs.

inputs.name: enabled
inputs.description: The whole switch. False makes this component a listener that files the event and does nothing — installed but harmless.

inputs.name: protectStoryCriticalUnits
inputs.description: Whether plot-essential characters get downed-instead-of-dead. True keeps the story finishable; false is the ironman promise and should be a separate visible toggle.

inputs.name: returnGearOnDeath
inputs.description: Whether equipped items return to inventory on loss. True softens the blow; false makes gearing a fallen unit a gamble, which some campaigns want.

outputs.name: fallenUnits
outputs.description: Roster of the permanently lost, for memorial UI and statistics.
